name: Bazin
subtitle: Bazin is a Libyan dough made from barley flour cooked in boiling salted water and served with a stew.

facts.label: What it is
facts.value: A Libyan barley-based dough served with a stew.

facts.label: Origin
facts.value: Originally a Berber dish; a classic family meal from Tripolitania, the historic north-western region of Libya.

facts.label: How it is cooked
facts.value: Barley flour is mixed into boiling salted water, cooked for at least an hour, then kneaded, divided and shaped into domes.

facts.label: How it is eaten
facts.value: Typically eaten by hand from a shared platter, with guests sitting on the ground around it.

facts.label: Change
facts.value: Volunteers in Tajura cook bazin for fasting people during Ramadan; one cook said that in the old days the dish was limited to the home.

parts.text: Bazin is a Libyan dough made from barley flour cooked in boiling salted water and served with a stew. The best-known version uses three parts barley flour to one part wheat flour; the cooked dough is kneaded and shaped into domes. It is an originally Berber (Amazigh) dish and a classic family meal from Tripolitania, in north-western Libya.

It is typically eaten by hand from a shared platter, often for lunch on Fridays, with stews that may feature lamb, camel meat, chicken, squid or broad beans; during Ramadan, volunteers in Tajura cook it for people breaking the fast.
